entities.summary:
Volkswagen AG is a German multinational automotive manufacturing corporation headquartered in Wolfsburg, founded in 1937 under the Nazi regime to produce the 'People's Car' (Volkswagen). Now the world's largest automaker by sales in multiple years, the Volkswagen Group encompasses 12 brands including VW, Audi, Porsche, Lamborghini, Bentley, SEAT, and Škoda.

The original Volkswagen Beetle, designed by Ferdinand Porsche with Nazi government support, was intended as affordable transportation for German workers but became, after WWII and particularly in 1960s America, an anti-establishment symbol embraced by the counterculture. VW's revival under British Army officer Ivan Hirst after WWII in devastated Wolfsburg, and subsequent transformation into West Germany's industrial champion, was a remarkable story of reconstruction.

The 2015 'Dieselgate' emissions scandal — when VW was found to have installed defeat devices allowing diesel cars to cheat emissions tests while emitting up to 40 times legal pollutant limits — was the largest corporate fraud in automotive history, resulting in $33 billion in fines, recalls, and settlements. The scandal accelerated the electric vehicle transition as VW committed to spending $100 billion on EV development through 2026.
